Below that is the following: "Biologists and taxonomists have made many attempts to define species, beginning when taxonomists such as Linnaeus had no option but to describe what they saw: the nominalist species concept. Ernst Mayr emphasized reproductive isolation, but this, like other definitions, is not always applicable or universally accepted. Later biologists have tried to refine Mayr's definition with the recognition and description of cryptic species, which are quite similar or overlap, so they are not easy to count: the biologist R.L. Mayden counted 22 species concepts; in 1997 the philosopher of science John Wilkins counted 26. [4] Wilkins further grouped the species concepts into (1) phenetic species based on overall similarity, (2) biospieces for reproductively isolated sexual organisms, (3) ecological species based on niche occupancy, (4) evolutionary species based on lineage (5) genetic species based on gene pool (6) morph species determined by a statistical difference, and (7) phylogenetic species a species as determined by a taxonomist.".
